messages.content: I need to retrieve server responses for certain user queries. Can you send a GET request to 'https://example.com/api/intent' for the following intents: ['get_balance', 'transfer_funds', 'hello', 'goodbye']? Here are the user queries that need to be matched with the intents: ['hello', 'I want to transfer funds'].

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the server's response. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent.

intents.description: A list of intent codes based on user queries, such as 'get_balance' and 'transfer_funds'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time in seconds to wait for the server response. The default is 2.5 seconds. This is a float type value.

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response, such as 'application/json'.

User-Agent.description: The user agent string of the software that is initiating the request, such as 'Mozilla/5.0'.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the GET request. If not provided, default headers will be used.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to send a GET request to https://example.com/api/intent with intents ['get_balance', 'transfer_funds', 'hello', 'goodbye']. They also provide user queries ['hello', 'I want to transfer funds'] that need to be matched with the intents. So we need to call the function get_response with url 'https://example.com/api/intent', intents ['get_balance', 'transfer_funds', 'hello', 'goodbye'], maybe also pass the user queries? The function signature only includes url, intents, timeout, headers. There's no field for user queries. But the user says "Here are the user queries that need to be matched with the intents". Possibly we just include them in the request body or query parameters? But the function only supports GET request. We can add query parameters via the URL. For example, we could append '?queries=hello,I want to transfer funds' or something. But the function signature doesn't allow specifying query parameters separately. We might encode them into the URL. But the function signature only has url string. So we can modify the URL to include query parameters. Let's do that.

We need to send a GET request to 'https://example.com/api/intent?intents=get_balance,transfer_funds,hello,goodbye&queries=hello,I want to transfer funds'.

But the function signature expects 'intents' as a separate argument. So we can pass intents=['get_balance','transfer_funds','hello','goodbye'] and maybe also pass queries? But there's no parameter for queries. So we can't pass them. But we can encode them into the URL. But the function signature only has url string. So we can embed the queries into the URL. But the function signature also has optional headers. We can set Accept: application/json, User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0. That is default.

Thus we call:

{
  "url": "https://example.com/api/intent?intents=get_balance,transfer_funds,hello,goodbye&queries=hello,I%20want%20to%20transfer%20funds",
  "intents": ["get_balance", "transfer_funds", "hello", "goodbye"],
  "timeout": 2.5,
  "headers": {
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"
  }
}

But the function signature says that if not provided, default headers will be used. So we don't need to specify headers. But we can still specify them.

We should call the function get_response with the arguments.
